finding: Round 10's `over-specification` finding (medium, regression) was recorded fixed with "the paragraph states an acceptance requirement rather than describing tool behaviour, and the description of what the check does moved to the guard document". Round 14 put tool description back into §7.1, and the fact now has three homes again — the exact count that finding named. spec/0.34.0.md:199-202 ("The check is deliberately **not** registered … it ran where the artifact does not yet exist"), spec/0.34.0-guard-tests.md:29-31 ("It is not a registered `workflow.checks` entry. Registered checks run during review, when this list does not exist yet…") and scripts/check-measured-claims.py:22-27 (docstring property 5) each state the registration status and the same rationale. They already disagree — "bought nothing" vs "bought a `PENDING` line every round", "every reviewer" vs "five reviewer roles" — which is §8.1's premise demonstrated inside the release that states it ("Four documents stating a fact means three of them will eventually be wrong"), and §8.1's cut rule ("Anything duplicated across two homes is cut from the non-owner") has already spent its one permitted overlap on the README command index. Drift between these same three homes has produced four recorded findings in this review already (rounds 10, 12, 13 mirror drift; round 14 half-applied repair). §7.1 also states the reason twice within itself: lines 193-195 already carry "registered `workflow.checks` run in the review phase only, while the list is written afterwards" as the justification for making the task the observer, and lines 199-202 restate it.

resolved.evidence: The general rule is corrected where it lives: section 8.1 now qualifies CLAUDE.md's register-the-check instruction by phase, and section 7.1 records only this release's instance. The guard document and the script docstring point at section 7.1 instead of restating the reason, so the fact has one home again.

suggestion: Keep in §7.1 only what the decomposer must act on — this release's task file does not register the check, and the first task's acceptance is the observer — and let the guard document keep the explanation, which is where round 10's repair put it. That removes the second statement of the same reason inside §7.1 and returns the fact to one home.

finding: The new closing paragraph states a durable, repo-wide convention — "a mechanical check earns its registration only in the phase where the thing it measures exists" — and explicitly marks it as general ("That is the general lesson, not a detail of this release"). By the spec's own placement rule this fact belongs to CLAUDE.md, which §8.1 assigns "this repository's own conventions and its self-development loop", and it amends a standing CLAUDE.md rule (register a mechanical check via workflow.checks once a class recurs) that this spec nowhere says it is changing. Instead it lives only in spec/0.34.0.md, which Non-Goal 6 classifies as a record rather than a living document ("Historical specs are records; the living docs were corrected and that is where correctness is maintained"). No section mandates carrying the lesson into an owning document, so §2's rule that an addition belongs here only when a section mandates it leaves the lesson generating no task and no owner: the one durable rule the round-14 edit adds is written in the one place the spec says is not maintained.

suggestion: Either (a) add the registration rule to §8.1's sweep as a fact CLAUDE.md must own — one line of acceptance, 'CLAUDE.md's checks rule states the phase condition' — so the general lesson has a maintained home, or (b) demote the paragraph to the release-local justification it actually is (this check was deregistered because the artifact does not exist during review) and delete the sentence that generalises it, leaving the standing CLAUDE.md rule untouched.

finding: The paragraph round 14 added to justify the retraction is disproven by measurement, in both of its load-bearing claims. §7.1 states that "registered `workflow.checks` run in the review phase only, while the list is written afterwards, so review would only ever see the check reporting `PENDING`" and that "the registration bought nothing: it ran where the artifact does not yet exist". Measured in a clone of dca0296 with the guard list UNWRITTEN — exactly today's state and exactly the state the sentence describes — the registered check exits 1, with no PENDING line, on eight distinct edits: the guard document's window moved to v0.31.2..v0.33.0; §7.1's own window moved; §7.1's window reworded past `between the \`<from>\` and \`<to>\` tags`; `--no-ext-diff` dropped from the documented command; the match rule reworded; the count made stale; the count reworded past its pattern; the guard document deleted. PENDING is the baseline state, not the only state — the four properties rounds 8, 9 and 10 built (spec-is-authority for the window, pinned command shape, pinned match rule, matchable count) all fire before the list logic is reached and are precisely the edits a review round makes: this review moved the window three times in rounds 2-5 and rewrote the count in round 5. So the registration did not buy nothing; it bought the guard against spec-side drift, and rounds 8/10 recorded high findings closed on exactly that. A third claim in the same sentence is also wrong as stated: "It was, for seven rounds" — the registration was added in 1d63b2c (the round-6 repair) and removed in bd3ba19 (the round-14 repair), and /tmp/tp-dev/r7..r14 prompt files all carry `do NOT report findings of these classes: code-citation-drift, measured-claim-not-reproducible`, so the class was suppressed for eight rounds (7 through 14), not seven; the script's own property 5 says "five reviewer roles" where the spec says "every reviewer". The retraction itself may still be right on the suppression ground alone, which is why this is medium: what is wrong is the recorded reason, and it is the reason §7.1 then generalises into a rule for future releases.

resolved.evidence: The rationale is narrowed to what measurement supports: the registration could never verify the list, but it did guard the window, rule and count claims, so the trade was real rather than free. The round count is corrected to eight.

suggestion: State the reason that survives measurement — the class-wide suppression of five reviewer roles cost more than the drift coverage the registration bought while the artifact did not exist — and drop "bought nothing", "would only ever see the check reporting PENDING" and the round count. If the drift coverage is to be kept, say who re-runs the check when §7.1's window or the guard document's numbers are edited during a review round, since from round 15 on nothing does.

finding: With the check deregistered, the first task's acceptance is its own sole observer, and the acceptance as written cannot distinguish a satisfied claim from an unmeasured one. Three conditions are stated as jointly reaching "exit 0 with no PENDING line": the list is written, it "matches the derivation as a set", and "the placeholder declaration is deleted". The PENDING line is what a placeholder declaration produces, so deleting that declaration is by itself sufficient to reach the stated pass condition; the spec never says what, after the deletion, still observes the set-equality condition. The result is an acceptance whose green state is reached both when the list is correctly derived and when nothing is left to check — the exact failure §2.2 defines as an artifact that does not discriminate, and the same shape as the silent-empty-list hazard the preceding paragraph warns about ("the task closes green over it"). Under the previous registered arrangement a later phase would at least re-run the check; nothing does now.

resolved.evidence: Measured against the current script rather than argued: deleting the placeholder declaration alone exits 1 with 'no list entries and no Populated by the first task declaration'. The tester's independent break attempt this round reached the same conclusion -- every constructed escape fails safe. The acceptance is not self-verifying.

suggestion: State which of the three conditions the script observes after the placeholder goes. Either keep a non-placeholder declaration that pins the derived set (or its count) so the check still fails when the file and the derivation disagree, or say plainly that set-equality is evidence the closing task must name under §2.1 rather than something the script proves — and in that case require the evidence to record the derivation command (with --no-ext-diff) and the resulting count, so a reader can re-run it.

finding: §7.1 now states a rule aimed past this release — "That is the general lesson, not a detail of this release — a mechanical check earns its registration only in the phase where the thing it measures exists" — and nothing routes it to the document that actually generates the behaviour. CLAUDE.md's self-development rules still say, unconditionally: "When `tp review --record` names the same `mechanize_candidates` class for a third round, write the check instead of the prose fix … register it with `tp set --workflow checks='[{\"class\":\"…\",\"cmd\":\"…\"}]'` and `tp review` runs it every round" — no phase condition, and registration is the whole instruction. So the next version's review loop follows CLAUDE.md and re-creates the registration §7.1 calls a mistake, while the lesson lives only in an archived version spec. This is the shape of two high findings this review already closed — round 3 `generator-recipe-not-updated` and round 5 `mask-regenerated-by-generator`, both resolved by making the CLAUDE.md/SKILL.md edit a stated constraint ("CLAUDE.md and skills/tp/SKILL.md drop the --quality-gate flag, without which the next init re-creates the override") — and it also inverts §8.1's own placement rule, which puts a fact in "the document the actor performing that task already has loaded" with pointers running toward the always-loaded document, never away from it. §8's sweep covers CLAUDE.md and §12 assigns no task for this edit.

resolved.evidence: The general rule is corrected where it lives: section 8.1 now qualifies CLAUDE.md's register-the-check instruction by phase, and section 7.1 records only this release's instance. The guard document and the script docstring point at section 7.1 instead of restating the reason, so the fact has one home again.

suggestion: Either make the CLAUDE.md edit an outcome of §8 (the mechanize rule gains the phase condition, and the v0.34.0 experience is its worked example), or drop the "general lesson" framing and state only what this release does with its own check — a rule with no durable home governs nothing.

finding: §8.2 states as measured that "observing emissions over this repository's own specs sees fewer than half the rules", and uses it to rule out observation as a source for the rule set. Re-derived, the number is exactly half, not fewer than half. `tp lint` can emit 16 distinct rules (heading-hierarchy, empty-section, duplicate-heading, orphan-reference, vague-language, section-size, long-spec, duplicate-line, numbering-gap, orphan-list-item, duplicate-paragraph, broken-cross-ref, structured-elements, frontmatter, acceptance-quality, affected-files-scope — the full call list in runLint). Running it over every `spec/*.md` in this repository emits 8 of them (structured-elements, acceptance-quality, vague-language, orphan-list-item, section-size, long-spec, orphan-reference, empty-section). 8/16 is the boundary the claim asserts it is under. The claim only becomes true under a denominator §8.2 never states — every rule any tp command can emit, including the `tp validate` and entry-rule families (~30) — and the README table this section repairs is explicitly a `tp lint` table, which is the denominator that falsifies it. A tester cannot write a pass/fail check for "fewer than half" when the corpus, the denominator and the command are all unstated and the two plausible denominators land on opposite sides of the inequality.

resolved.evidence: Section 8.2 states no fraction at all. Two rounds put one in that sentence -- a third, then fewer than half -- and both were wrong; the argument never needed the figure.

suggestion: State the measurement so it reproduces, or drop the ratio. Either write it as a bounded fact — "linting every `spec/*.md` emits 8 of the 16 rules `tp lint` can emit" — or replace it with the qualitative claim the argument actually needs: "observation over this repository's own specs exercises only part of the rule set, so it cannot source the complete one." The conclusion survives either way; the number as written does not.

finding: The Overview table's bulk-reader Consequence cell states a specific measured outcome — "A 3-row file with one 70KB line adds one task and discards two, reporting success" — without pinning which row is over-long, and the outcome is entirely determined by that unstated detail. Measured against today's tree with `tp add --bulk` on a 3-row NDJSON file: over-long line at row 1 → 0 added, exit 0; at row 2 → 1 added, exit 0 (the stated outcome); at row 3 → 2 added, exit 0. bufio.Scanner stops at the over-long token, so the count added is the number of rows *before* it, not a fixed one. Two engineers building the fixture for the §4 regression from this row therefore observe three different pre-fix behaviours, and only one of them reproduces the sentence the spec presents as a fact.

resolved.evidence: Section 1's row states the behaviour rather than a row count: the over-long line and every row after it are discarded. The previous wording was true only when the long line sat in the middle.

suggestion: Pin the position in the cell — "a 3-row file whose second row is 70KB adds one task and discards two, reporting success" — or state the invariant instead of one instance: "every row after the over-long one is discarded and the command still exits 0."

finding: "`-race` roughly doubles test wall time" does not reproduce on this tree. Measured with warm build caches on the repo's own suite: `go test ./... -count=1` at 16.71s / 15.68s / 15.58s, `go test -race ./... -count=1` at 18.85s / 18.87s / 23.46s — a ratio of 1.13x to 1.51x, median ~1.2x, not ~2x. The suite is dominated by process spawn and file I/O rather than instrumented compute, so the race detector's usual factor does not apply here. Now that `measured-claim-not-reproducible` is no longer mechanized, this is the one number in the spec that no guard covers and that a reader can falsify in two commands; it is also the number an operator would use to judge whether the gate change is affordable.

resolved.evidence: Section 5 states the measured range, between a tenth and a half again of wall time, rather than roughly double.

suggestion: Either drop the multiplier and say the gate gets measurably slower without quantifying it, or state the figure that reproduces — e.g. "`-race` adds roughly 20-50% to test wall time on this suite (measured 15.6s to 18.9s)" — and name the derivation (`go test ./... -count=1` vs `go test -race ./... -count=1`, warm cache) so a later round can re-run it.

finding: Round 14's `fixed-repair-half-applied` (low, regression) was recorded fixed with "The stale docstring property is replaced by the one that is now true: the check is deliberately unregistered." Verified against the shipped script rather than the evidence line: property 5 was rewritten (scripts/check-measured-claims.py:22-27), but the paragraph nine lines below it still justifies itself by the registration that property 5 says does not exist — check-measured-claims.py:31-32 reads "It prints on every run, because the registration tells every reviewer to stop reporting the whole class." The docstring therefore both asserts and denies the registration, and the surviving sentence is the argument FOR re-registering, which is what §7.1:199-202 exists to forbid; line 4 ("Mechanizes the `measured-claim-not-reproducible` review class") reads the same way. This is the third consecutive round in which a repair to this docstring landed on one sentence and left an adjacent one describing the removed state (round 13 `retired-guard-residue`, round 14 `fixed-repair-half-applied`, now). Harm is contained — nothing parses the docstring and the check behaves correctly (22 mutations re-run this round against dca0296: the full 100-entry list with the declaration deleted exits 0 with no PENDING; a 99-entry, fabricated, duplicated, misplaced-under-any-heading-level, hidden-above-heading, stale-count, reworded-rule, moved-window, dropped-flag, deleted-document or empty list all exit 1) — which is why this is low.
